title: Wi-Fi Security & Public Wi-Fi Policy Template
metaDescription: Complete policy template for safe public Wi-Fi usage. Protect against man-in-the-middle attacks, evil twins, and data theft on hotel and cafe networks.
description: A comprehensive policy template to establish secure Wi-Fi usage guidelines for organizations and individuals. Covers public Wi-Fi risks, security protocols, and best practices to prevent data breaches and cyber attacks on unsecured networks.

sections.heading: Purpose and Scope
sections.content: This Wi-Fi Security Policy establishes guidelines for secure wireless network usage by {{organization_name}} personnel. This policy applies to all employees, contractors, and visitors accessing public Wi-Fi networks or connecting to our corporate wireless infrastructure. The purpose is to protect sensitive data from interception, prevent unauthorized network access, and mitigate security risks associated with wireless communications.

sections.heading: Public Wi-Fi Security Requirements
sections.content: When connecting to public Wi-Fi networks in hotels, cafes, airports, or other public venues, users must: 1) Verify network authenticity with venue staff before connecting, 2) Use a reputable VPN service for all internet traffic, 3) Avoid accessing sensitive accounts or conducting financial transactions, 4) Enable two-factor authentication on all accounts, 5) Use privacy-focused browsers like a privacy-focused browser to minimize tracking, 6) Disable automatic Wi-Fi connection and file sharing features. Users must never connect to networks with suspicious names or those requesting excessive personal information during sign-up.

sections.heading: Prohibited Activities on Public Networks
sections.content: The following activities are strictly prohibited when connected to public Wi-Fi: accessing company databases or sensitive systems without VPN protection, transmitting confidential information in unencrypted formats, downloading or installing software from untrusted sources, connecting to networks with names like 'Free WiFi' or generic hotspot names that may be evil twin attacks, sharing network credentials with unauthorized individuals, and leaving devices unattended while connected. Violation of these guidelines may result in disciplinary action and potential security incidents.

sections.heading: Corporate Wi-Fi Security Standards
sections.content: {{organization_name}} wireless networks implement WPA3 encryption as the minimum security standard. Network access requires authentication through {{auth_method}} and periodic password updates every {{password_cycle}} days. Guest networks are isolated from corporate resources and have restricted internet access. All wireless traffic is monitored for suspicious activity, and devices must comply with our endpoint security requirements including up-to-date antivirus software and operating system patches.

sections.heading: Incident Reporting and Response
sections.content: Users must immediately report suspected security incidents to the IT security team at {{security_email}} or {{security_phone}}. This includes connecting to potentially malicious networks, receiving security warnings, suspicious pop-ups or certificate errors, unexpected requests for credentials, or any indication of compromised accounts. Upon reporting, users should disconnect from the network, run security scans, and change passwords for any accounts accessed during the session. The security team will investigate incidents within {{response_time}} hours and provide remediation guidance.

sections.heading: Compliance and Enforcement
sections.content: Compliance with this Wi-Fi Security Policy is mandatory for all {{organization_name}} personnel. Regular security awareness training will be provided covering public Wi-Fi risks, safe connection practices, and threat identification. IT will conduct periodic audits of wireless security configurations and user compliance. Violations may result in network access suspension, mandatory retraining, or disciplinary action depending on severity. This policy will be reviewed annually and updated to address emerging threats and technology changes.
